findings.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — Raw `new Thread` runs a tight busy-loop with no sleep/backoff and no join(), so it can leak and keep spinning past the test's lifetime if an earlier assertion (e.g. group creation failure at line 129/131) throws before `deletedAll.set(true)` is reached

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — Raw `new Thread` runs a tight busy-loop with no sleep/backoff and no join(), so it can leak and keep spinning past the test's lifetime if an earlier assertion (e.g. group creation failure at line 129/131) throws before `deletedAll.set(true)` is reached

adjudication.rationale: The added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a raw `new Thread` that runs `while (!deletedAll.get()) { managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...); }` with no sleep/backoff and the thread is never joined or stopped via `finally`. If any exception/early test failure occurs after the thread starts but before `deletedAll.set(true)` (e.g., during deletion or other unexpected runtime exceptions), the thread can keep spinning beyond the test lifetime. Even on success, lack of `join()` means the thread may still be running when the final assertion executes, creating flakiness and unnecessary load.
